A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anti-oestrogents stimulate the shedding of the extracytoplasmic domain of ERBB2, which may be one of the mechanisms for resistance of ERBB2 overexpressing breast tumours to anti-oestrogent treatment.

The main takeaway from our work is that
anti-oestrogic stimulation of ERBB-2 ectodomain release may be a mechanism of resistance to anti-oestrogen treatment in breast cancer cells with amplified ERBB-2.
the ERBB2 gene is not only regulated by transcription, but also by proteolysis of the ERBB-2 protein.
